_doc: Farhold's crafting. There is no mining and no woodcutting — every material in the game comes out of an item you recycled, or off a chest, a champion, a rare or a boss. THREE materials, one per rung of the rarity ladder, because twelve was a list nobody could hold in their head: Scrap Iron from anything, Bound Essence from magic and rare gear, Resonant Dust only from legendaries and the things that are hard to kill. Advanced work needs the advanced material — that is the whole progression.

scrap.name: Scrap Iron
scrap.desc: Bent fittings, broken buckles, cut straps. Everything you recycle gives some of this.

essence.name: Bound Essence
essence.desc: What is left when a magic property is pulled apart. Magic and rare gear gives it; so do champions.

dust.name: Resonant Dust
dust.desc: Only a legendary grinds this fine, and only a rare or a boss carries any. Everything worth doing costs it.

_salvageDoc: What recycling an item gives back, by rarity. Better gear gives better material and more of it; quality adds a little on top; a unique or a set piece always leaves dust behind whatever else it rolls.
_harvestDoc: What a body leaves behind. Ordinary things give scrap; a champion is worth an essence; a rare and a boss are where dust comes from.
_recipeDoc: The bench, in two halves. `kind: create` makes something new and lives on the Crafting tab; everything else reworks an item you already have and lives on the Upgrade tab. `minRarity`/`slot`/`minLevel` gate an action to items it makes sense on. Costs scale with the item's level band (js/craft.js `bandCost`), so reworking a level-28 weapon is not the price of a level-2 one.

recipes.name: Forge a weapon
recipes.desc: Beat scrap into a plain weapon of your level. Pick exactly which one — it comes out normal, and magic find can carry it higher.

recipes.name: Forge armour
recipes.desc: A plain piece of armour of your level, in whichever slot you need filling.

recipes.name: Bind a quiver
recipes.desc: Hide, thread and twenty heads. Pick which kind — the plain one adds damage to every arrow, and the special ones brand them, split them, steer them or make them burst.

recipes.name: Cast a trinket
recipes.desc: A ring or an amulet. Trinkets roll an extra property, so this is the cheapest way to a useful magic item.

recipes.name: Forge a fine piece
recipes.desc: The same work done properly: rare, with three properties on it.

recipes.name: Forge a masterwork
recipes.desc: Everything you have, spent on one piece. Legendary, with five or six properties.

recipes.name: Temper
recipes.desc: Raise the item's quality one step. Every number on it goes up — damage, armour and every property together.

recipes.name: Reinforce
recipes.desc: Beat extra plate into the piece: a quarter more armour, permanently. Up to three times.

recipes.name: Hone
recipes.desc: A fifth more damage on the base itself, before any property. Up to three times.

recipes.name: Promote
recipes.desc: Push the item up a rarity and roll it a new property with the room that makes.

recipes.name: Inscribe
recipes.desc: Add one more property, if the item has a slot free for it.

recipes.name: Reweave one property
recipes.desc: Trade one property you do not want for a different one. Each reweave of the same item costs more than the last.

recipes.name: Re-roll the numbers
recipes.desc: Keep every property, roll their values again. The cheap, safe way to fix a bad roll.

recipes.name: Recast every property
recipes.desc: Throw the whole set back and roll it again. The gamble — it can come out worse.

recipes.name: Brand with fire
recipes.desc: Your hits set light to what they touch.

recipes.name: Brand with rime
recipes.desc: Your hits leave the target slowed.

recipes.name: Brand with void
recipes.desc: Your hits eat away at what they land on.

_groupDoc: How the Upgrade tab sorts its list.
_bandDoc: How much dearer the work gets as the item's level rises. A band is five levels.
